newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-SCALA SAYS HAD TALKS WITH BORUSSIA DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SCALA SAYS HAD TALKS WITH BORUSSIA DORTMUND.

text.p: Nevio Scala, coach of recently-relegated Italian club Perugia, said on Wednesday that he had been approached by Germany's European Cup holders Borussia Dortmund.

"I cannot deny it, there has been this contact," he told the daily Gazzetta dello Sport. "The prospect of coaching the strongest team in Europe is wonderful, it's cause for pride to know that they are thinking of me in Dortmund."
However, Scala, who joined Perugia this year after former coach Giovanni Galeone was sacked, has a contract with the central Italian club until the year 2000.
He said also that other clubs were interested in him, including Spain's Tenerife.

Dortmund are looking for a new coach after Ottmar Hitzfeld quit this month, just nine days after the club beat Juventus 3-1 in the European Cup final in Munich. Hitzfeld has said he is taking over as sports director at the club.
Scala enjoyed seven successful years at Parma before being replaced there by current coach Carlo Ancelotti.
If he were to move to Dortmund he would be the second Italian coach in the Bundesliga, alongside Giovanni Trapattoni who guided Bayern Munich to the league title last season.
